response.text: {"intro":"Fernwood Labs builds developer tools for engineering teams. It has 14 people in 5 teams and runs on Bike with six apps: Hiring, Tools and budgets, Onboarding, Spend, Time off and Customer contracts. Each one is a set of sheets, the steps a row moves through, and who can see and do what.","paragraphs":["Fernwood Labs has 14 people in 5 teams, and every person has a manager on record. The apps use this list to fill in fields such as hiring manager, tool owner, expense employee and contract owner. Time off also uses it to find the manager who approves a request.","At Fernwood Labs a person's path starts in Hiring. Candidates move from Applied through Phone screen, Interview and Offer to Hired or Rejected. Each interviewer is asked for a scorecard from 1 to 4 on the day of the interview. If an offer is above the top of the salary band, Wade must approve it before it is sent. When a candidate is Hired, the opening is marked Filled and a first-week plan starts in Onboarding. Aisha is asked to pick a buddy, Jon gets an IT task for the laptop, accounts and software seats, and the manager and buddy get tasks too. When the plan enters First week, a row for the starter's software seats is added to Tools.","Fernwood Labs tracks its software in Tools and budgets. Each tool has an owner and a renewal date. Thirty days before the renewal date the tool moves to Renewal due and the owner gets an email. If the tool costs more than $5,000 a year, Wade is asked to approve or decline the renewal. Budgets are set per team and quarter, and the Spent and Left figures are worked out from approved and paid expenses.","Spending at Fernwood Labs goes through three sheets in Spend. Expenses need a receipt and a category before they can be approved, and the person who asked cannot approve their own expense. If the receipt is missing, the employee is asked to attach one. Once it is there, Lena is asked to approve or reject it, and she is told when it is ready to be paid with the next payroll. Purchases over $2,000 go to Krishna for approval, and smaller ones go to Lena. Renewal requests go to the budget owner to approve or decline.","Fernwood Labs earns its revenue from the contracts in Customer contracts. Each contract has a yearly value, a renewal date and a notice period. Contracts over $50,000 go through Legal review before they are signed. Sixty days before the notice date, an active contract moves to Renewal due and its owner is asked to act. If nobody has acted 30 days before the notice date, Wade and the owner are emailed. A renewal request is also started in Spend for the budget owner to decide.","Time off at Fernwood Labs is handled in Time off, and the calendar includes 10 public holidays. Employees ask for leave, and the manager approves or declines it. Vacation can only be requested when the days are within the days left. Approved leave moves to Taken the day after the last day, and vacation days are then taken off the balance through a new entry. Entries can only be added or reversed, never changed, and a balance cannot go below 0.","Much of the work at Fernwood Labs runs by itself. The apps hold 29 rules that move rows along, send emails and ask named people to decide. Wade approves high offers and large tool renewals, Lena and Krishna approve spending, and managers approve leave. Every change, made by hand or through Customize, is recorded in the Audit log."],"sentences":[{"capability":"Hiring","sentence":"Holds candidates, openings and interviews; Wade manages everything, hiring managers handle their own candidates and openings, and interviewers fill in their own interviews."},{"capability":"Tools and budgets","sentence":"Holds the software tools with owners, costs and renewal dates, and the budgets per team and quarter; Wade and Lena manage tools and owners see their own."},{"capability":"Onboarding","sentence":"Holds first-week plans and their tasks for new starters; Wade and Aisha manage the plans, and task owners and plan managers see their own work."},{"capability":"Spend","sentence":"Holds expenses, purchases and renewal requests; everyone adds their own expenses and purchases, Lena approves most of them, Krishna approves large purchases and Wade manages the app."},{"capability":"Time off","sentence":"Holds leave requests and the leave entries that keep each person's balance; employees ask for leave, managers decide, and Lena adds entries."},{"capability":"Customer contracts","sentence":"Holds customer contracts with value, renewal date and notice period; Wade and Krishna manage all contracts and owners handle their own."}],"phrases":[{"connection":"Hiring > Onboarding","phrase":"when someone is hired, their first week is planned"},{"connection":"Spend > Tools and budgets","phrase":"approved and paid expenses are added up as spent in the budget"},{"connection":"Onboarding > Tools and budgets","phrase":"when a first week starts, software seats are added for the new starter"},{"connection":"Customer contracts > Spend","phrase":"when a contract is due for renewal, a renewal request is started"}],"worth":["18 expenses have no Category, which matters because an expense cannot be approved until its category is filled in.","Tool renewals above $5,000 go to Wade, while customer renewal requests go to the budget owner, so the two renewal paths follow different rules.","Onboarding has no plans yet, so the hand-off from Hiring to Onboarding has not been used."]}
